assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a whole class of matter defined by topology rather than symmetry breaking. Theory (Kane-Mele) predicted it, and the HgTe quantum-well experiment gave a clean, falsifiable confirmation. Impact on condensed matter, materials and quantum devices is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical contribution (Z2 classification, spin-orbit quantum spin Hall). Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation in HgTe. This gives a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal), Fu and Kane (3D), and Hasan and the ARPES groups are outside the supplied credit, which is a real allocation concern.
assessment.maturity: Strongly mature: about two decades of independent confirmation, many material platforms, and a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely or somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the 2D quantum spin Hall result alone sufficient without the 3D topological insulator discoveries, which this candidate omits.
The credited set omits Zhang (deceased) and others whose contributions to the HgTe proposal were decisive; I cannot independently verify the priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and was a landmark instrument-driven discovery. It required unprecedented detector, trigger and data-analysis engineering at the LHC. Its importance is not in doubt.
assessment.attribution: The theory was recognised in 2013. The experimental discovery rests on thousands of collaborators; the three credited names are founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS, which is a defensible but inherently imperfect way to honour a collaboration discovery. The statutes allow individuals only, and this configuration highlights detector conception and leadership rather than the analysis itself.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: confirmed by two independent experiments and by Run 2 coupling and spin-parity measurements. Timing is arguably long overdue for the experimental side.
uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts spokesperson and founder credit as capturing the decisive contributions in a very large collaboration.
Other individuals (e.g. early-concept proponents, analysis and detector leaders, accelerator leaders) have strong claims; the allocation is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised to remarkable accuracy by Ye's group, improved time and frequency standards by orders of magnitude. They enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and prospects for redefining the second. This is an instrument-and-measurement achievement of exactly the type that gives lasting value.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice approach; Ye's group pushed it to the 10^-18 regime and developed associated spectroscopy and comparison technology. Two laureates is a clean configuration. Other groups (Hall and Hansch precursor prize, Hollberg, Ludlow, Lemonde, Ovsiannikov and Takamoto) contributed but the supplied credit is a sensible core.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent labs reproduce and exceed accuracy, and international redefinition planning is under way. Timely.
uncertainties: Competition from trapped-ion clock work (Wineland prize overlap, 2012) may make the committee view the field as partly recognised.
Redefinition of the second has not yet occurred; some may prefer to wait.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity, launching moire and twistronics research. The originality of the theory-experiment connection and the volume of follow-on work are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experiments (2018). Cao and others in his group and Dean's hBN-encapsulation contributions, plus earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto theory, complicate priority, but the supplied trio is a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature for a field about eight years old: reproduced widely, though mechanisms of superconductivity and correlated states remain debated. Possibly slightly early compared with the strongest candidates.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled, so the interpretation is not fully stable.
Priority between Lopes dos Santos et al. and Bistritzer-MacDonald is not resolved by the supplied credit; I am not able to verify this independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned quantum many-body models into controllable experiments (Mott insulator transition, single-site quantum-gas microscopy). This created a general-purpose analogue quantum simulation platform with large reach in condensed matter and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposal for Bose-Hubbard physics in lattices; Greiner and Bloch realised the Mott transition and developed quantum-gas microscopy. Cirac is also credited in the longlist but I choose a three-person configuration. Hänsch, Kasevich, Esslinger and Bakr also have claims, and Ketterle and Cornell/Wieman were earlier recognised for BEC.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of replication across many laboratories and species, and now routinely used for quantum simulation. Timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with other Zoller-Cirac candidates may split the credit; whether the committee prefers the theory-led pairing instead (Cirac and Zoller) is open.
Quantum-gas microscopy credit is shared among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts fixed their cosmological distances and ended a long debate about their origin. It laid the foundation for GRB science and multi-messenger transients. I note that I work on gamma-ray instrumentation and polarimetry, and I have taken that into account by judging this on the evidence only.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow in 1997; Kulkarni's group led the optical, redshift and radio follow-up. Contributions by van Paradijs, Groot, Djorgovski, Metzger and Frail were also decisive and complicate a three-person split.
assessment.maturity: Mature: nearly three decades, with extensive independent confirmation and an established fireball model. Not premature.
uncertainties: Several credible alternative laureates (van Paradijs, deceased, would be excluded; Djorgovski and Frail are not credited here).
Allocation between satellite discovery and ground-based follow-up is genuinely disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP provided a precision map of CMB anisotropies and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent-level precision, establishing the flat Lambda-CDM paradigm. Its impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as principal investigator, Page led instrument design and calibration, and Spergel led the cosmological analysis. This is a sensible instrument-plus-interpretation split, though the mission team was large.
assessment.maturity: Mature: confirmed and superseded by Planck, with consistent parameters. A question is whether the committee considers CMB cosmology already honoured (2006 COBE, 2019 Peebles).
uncertainties: Incremental over COBE in principle, and Planck refined it; the committee may view the discovery as partly already recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. This was an instrumental feat, a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice, and a genuine new window on the cosmos. I note a professional proximity to astroparticle instrumentation and have judged on the evidence.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; a single laureate is feasible but ignores the roles of other leaders in the collaboration and of AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES precursors, and of the theory that anticipated the flux. The supplied credit offers only one name, so no alternative configuration is available.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: the diffuse flux is firmly established, source identifications are at 3-4 sigma level with confirmation by KM3NeT and others still developing. Possibly slightly early for source astronomy.
uncertainties: Source-level evidence is not yet at discovery significance for most claims, and independent confirmation is limited.
A single-laureate configuration may be seen as an unfair attribution for a large collaboration.
